$comment: Every wording a reason had before verdicts kept their facts (tools/reasons_past.py collects them from the commits without 30ee5f1; newest first). agentcake/detect/reasons_past.py matches a kept sentence against these to read its facts back, so that it is worded anew. Not interface text: never shown.

exclude.prefetch: Page {page} was requested as a {purpose}: its server half doesn't count.
Page {page} was requested as a {purpose}: its server half is not used.
exclude.never-shown: Page {page} was prerendered and never shown, so it doesn't count.
Page {page} was prerendered and never shown: it is left out.
exclude.all: Every page was prerendered and never shown: not a visit.
name.ua-generic: The User-Agent of {half} names {name}, a tool anyone can run: it names no agent product.
name.ua-conflict: The User-Agent of {half} declares several names at once, {names}, so none of them counts.
The User-Agent of {half} declares several names at once ({names}): none of them is used.
name.ua-hint: The User-Agent has the shape of a forged or malformed one, {hint}: a weak signal.
The User-Agent has the shape of a forged or malformed one ({hint}): a weak signal.
name.signer: Signature-Agent on {half} names {signer}, the signer of {name}.
name.unknown-signer: Signature-Agent on {half} names {signer}, which isn't among the signers that come with this release.
Signature-Agent on {half} names {signer}, which is not among the signers that come with this release.
name.disagree: The declared names, {names}, disagree, so the visit gets no name.
The declared names disagree ({names}): no name is given.
name.signer-mismatch: Signature-Agent names {claimed}, but the signature belongs to {signer}.
name.outranked: {other} ({other_method}) gives way to {name} ({method}), which comes first.
name.from-trace: This trace belongs to {name}: likely {name}, since a trace can change when the product updates.
verify.signature-forged: {detail} It claims to be {name}: impersonation, so the visit gets no name.
{detail} It claims to be {name}: impersonation, so no name is given.
verify.signature-proxy: {detail} The signature covers {components}, which a proxy in front of the site may rewrite: couldn't verify, not impersonation.
{detail} The signature covers {components}, which a proxy in front of the site may rewrite: could not verify, not impersonation.
verify.ip-range: The address is in {range}, which {operator} publishes for {name}: verified.
verify.ip-agent-range: The address is in {range}, which {operator} publishes for its agents.
verify.ip-bot-range: The address is in {range}, which {operator} publishes for its crawlers, but nothing declares a name.
verify.ip-mismatch: It says it's {name}, but the address isn't in the ranges {operator} publishes for it: impersonation, so the visit gets no name.
It says it is {name}, but the address is not in the ranges {operator} publishes for it: impersonation, so no name is given.
verify.rdns-mismatch: It says it's {name}, but reverse DNS doesn't confirm it: impersonation, so the visit gets no name.
It says it is {name}, but reverse DNS does not confirm it: impersonation, so no name is given.
verify.no-range: {name} publishes no address range or key that {product} can check: self-reported only.
verify.local: Local mode: every visit comes from 127.0.0.1, so there's no verification layer and names are self-reported only.
Local mode: every visit comes from 127.0.0.1, so there is no verification layer and names are self-reported only.
verify.no-address: No visitor address was available, so the check against the published ranges didn't run: names are self-reported only.
No visitor address was available, so the published ranges were not checked: names are self-reported only.
env.automated: Automated browser: it may be an AI tool working for a human, or a script.
env.cloud-browser: A cloud browser that doesn't say who runs it
A cloud browser that does not say who runs it.
env.extension-unnamed: An extension acted on this page, but nothing says which one.
env.soft-alone: There's only soft environment evidence, such as DevTools or privacy tools, which a human's browser can also show, and that isn't enough on its own.
Only soft environment evidence, which a human's browser can also show (DevTools, privacy tools): not enough on its own.
behavior.agent: The behavior model judged the session an agent's: {basis}.
The behavior model judged the session an agent's ({agent_pct}% of the actions).
behavior.human: The behavior model judged the session a human's, with {human_pct}% of the action segments.
The behavior model judged the session a human's ({human_pct}% of the action segments).
The behavior model judged the session a human's ({human_pct}% of the actions).
behavior.one-kind: Only one kind of behavior looks like an agent's: {kind}. The behavior model needs two independent kinds before it judges a session an agent's.
behavior.unsure: The behavior model couldn't tell a human from an agent, with {unsure_pct}% of the action segments unsure.
The behavior model could not tell a human from an agent ({unsure_pct}% of the action segments unsure).
The behavior model could not tell a human from an agent ({unsure_pct}% of the actions unsure).
behavior.indicator: {words}: the actions in that time are the agent's.
behavior.handoff: The {to} took over from the {from} {at} s into the session.
behavior.short-run: A {who} run of {n} actions in {span} s is too short to count as a {who} taking part.
behavior.overruled: The behavior model saw a human, but behavior doesn't overturn automation traces.
The behavior model saw a human, but behavior does not overturn automation traces.
behavior.assistive: Keyboard navigation without a pointer, as assistive tools do: the behavior model's agent judgment isn't trusted.
Keyboard navigation without a pointer, as assistive tools do: the behavior model's agent judgment is not trusted.
Keyboard navigation without a pointer, as assistive tools do: the behavior model's agent judgement is not trusted.
behavior.local-agent: There's no agent trace in the page or the browser, only behavior, so it's possibly an agent on the visitor's own computer.
No agent trace in the page or the browser, only behavior: possibly an agent on the visitor's own computer.
behavior.too-little-data: There are too few actions for the behavior model, {n} of the {min} it needs, so it doesn't judge the session.
Too few actions for the behavior model ({n} of the {min} it needs): not judged.
behavior.touch: A phone or tablet: the behavior model isn't used.
A phone or tablet: the behavior model is not used.
behavior.not-run-bot: A listed bot, known by name: the behavior model doesn't run.
A listed bot, known by name: the behavior model is not run.
crawler.like: Looks like a crawler: {signals}. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.timezone-country: The browser's time zone, {tz}, isn't one used in {country}, the country of its address. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
The browser's time zone ({tz}) is not one used in the country of its address ({country}). A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.language-country: None of the browser's languages, {languages}, names {country}, the country of its address. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
None of the browser's languages ({languages}) names the country of its address ({country}). A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.same-address: {n} sessions came from this address within {hours} h. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.header-order: The User-Agent says {browser}, but cake.js's requests list their headers in an order {browser} doesn't use: {order}. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
The User-Agent says {browser}, but cake.js's requests list their headers in an order {browser} does not use ({order}). A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.display-change: The screen changed during the session: color depth {depths}, size {sizes}. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
The screen changed during the session (color depth {depths}; size {sizes}). A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.window-jump: The window jumped {px} px across the screen without changing its size. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.rhythm-pauses: {pct}% of the steps came after at least {seconds} s without any input, as when an AI looks at the page before it acts. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
weak.rhythm-no-pause: {pct}% of the steps came right after the previous one, as a script runs them. A weak signal: it changes nothing.
